scenes.title: Recruit for relevance
scenes.narration: Recruit people with recent relevant experience, not just people who like your idea. Start with your learning question and conversation guide. This lesson prepares a plan; it sends no invitations.

scenes.title: Check fit with minimal questions
scenes.narration: Define who is relevant and why. Ask a neutral screening question about recent context. Avoid collecting identities or sensitive details you do not need. Exclusions should relate to the research question.

scenes.title: Use permitted access
scenes.visual: Founder requests a fictional gatekeeper approval
scenes.narration: Choose an appropriate channel and confirm permission to use it. Membership of a group does not automatically authorise harvesting contacts or sending bulk messages. Mark access as pending until confirmed.

scenes.title: Make the invitation clear
scenes.narration: Explain the purpose, time, activity and contact route. Make it easy to decline or stop. Separate any recording request. State any incentive honestly and do not tie it to positive feedback or a purchase.

scenes.title: Track honestly
scenes.narration: Invited, replied, eligible, scheduled and completed are different statuses. A target is not a recruited participant. Agree permitted follow-up, accept no response and avoid repeated pressure. Do not fabricate responses.

scenes.title: Preserve limits
scenes.narration: Plan variation across relevant contexts and record who your channels miss. A convenience sample does not represent an entire market. Keep personal contacts outside this prototype; assign privacy and retention review before recruitment.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Invite people who can help you learn.

children: Participant fit
means relevant experience in the context you want to understand.
Screening
checks that fit with a few neutral questions.
Sampling limits
describe who your chosen channels may miss.
Relevant experience
For a registration study: adults who recently registered for the type of event you are exploring, including those whose current process worked well.
Selection bias
Only asking friends who admire your idea can hide disagreement. Add another permitted channel and record the remaining limits.
Start with Lesson 26’s learning question and guide.
Define experience/context criteria before choosing people.
Use minimal neutral screening; avoid sensitive personal details.
Confirm channel and gatekeeper permission.
Explain purpose, time, choice and any incentive clearly.
Track access honestly; accept decline or silence without pressure.
Illustrative invitation

“I’m learning how adults recently handled event registration. Would you consider a 20-minute conversation about your experience? Participation is optional; you can skip questions or stop. There is no purchase required. We will discuss recording separately before any recording. Please use the approved contact route if interested.”
Adapt the activity, time, contact route, privacy explanation and incentive to the actual approved plan. Do not promise confidentiality you cannot deliver.

A planning target is not a statistical sample-size claim. A small convenience sample helps explore experiences but does not establish market-wide percentages. Contact lists, identities and recordings belong in an approved secure system, not this local worksheet. Work with adults here; research involving minors or sensitive topics needs a separate reviewed process.
Review neutral conversation guide
